newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia new bond at 6.79/81 pct ahead of issue.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia new bond at 6.79/81 pct ahead of issue.

text.p: Malaysia's new government bond was trading at a pre-issue yield of 6.79 to 6.81 percent ahead of the tender's results on Thursday, dealers said.
Bank Negara will announce the results of the issue on behalf of the government and the issue is on Friday.
The dealers said the two-billion ringgit, 10-year government bond issue has been over the last few days been converging to a consensus 6.8 percent average yield.
"There is very strong support at 6.8 percent level; results should be targetting that area," said a dealer with a local bank in Kuala Lumpur.
Banks in Malaysia began trading the bond, or Malaysian Government Security (MGS), soon after the issue was announced last week.
This is the third MGS issue this year. In June, Bank Negara, on behalf of the government, raised two billion ringgit from the issue of five-year bonds at a coupon of 6.48 percent.
In September, it issued seven-year government bonds to raise two billion ringgit at a coupon of 6.586 percent.

Dealers said the latest bond issue would mop up liquidity arising from some large Bank Negara bill and deposit maturities and roll over two maturing MGS issues totalling 1.1 billion ringgit on December 15.
